title: A Memory-Efficient Hierarchical Algorithm for Large-scale Optimal Transport Problems
claim: Solve a large problem coarse-to-fine, reusing each coarse solution as the start for a few cheap restricted refinement steps per level.
layout: Stacked scale rows, top-to-bottom, left-to-right flow, dashed prolongation arrows, legend inset
description: A multi-scale pipeline diagram with three stacked rows for Scale L, Scale L-1 and Scale 0, joined by chevrons on the left. Each row starts with a pair of grayscale images (cameraman and Lena) overlaid with grids that get finer at lower scales, labeled u and v. At Scale L, a PDHG solver produces a purple-yellow transport plan heatmap. A dashed arrow carries it down to Scale L-1, where it enters a dashed rounded box labeled ×O(1). Inside, a loop alternates update (filled arrows) and solve (hollow arrows) steps, with a sparse active-set heatmap N between them. A second dashed arrow labeled coarse-to-fine prolongation links Scale L-1 to Scale 0, which repeats the same loop and ends in Output. A grey legend box in the top right explains solveRestricted, updateActive and prolongation. Blue palette throughout.
caption: Architecture of HALO.
abstract: We propose HALO, a memory-efficient hierarchical algorithm for solving large-scale optimal transport (OT) problems with squared Euclidean cost, particularly effective in moderate-dimensional settings. The core of \ours lies in combining a hierarchical representation of the OT problem with parallel-friendly linear programming solvers, within which an active pruning technique is integrated to further reduce memory usage and computational cost. Theoretically, we establish a scale-independent iteration-complexity upper bound for the refinement phase, which is consistent with our numerical observations. Numerically, experiments on the image dataset \dataset and the 3D point cloud dataset \datasetnongrid demonstrate that \ours effectively alleviates the memory and scalability bottlenecks of existing solvers. Our method demonstrates significant advantages compared to state-of-the-art baselines: for images with $n=1024^2$ pixels, it achieves an $8.9\times$ speedup and $70.5$% reduction in memory usage under comparable accuracy; for 3D point clouds at scale $n=2^{18}$, it achieves a $1.84\times$ speedup and an $83.2$% reduction in memory usage with $24.9$% lower transport cost.
